candidates.explanation: Board clearly owns orchestration and policy, uses board-local ports with adapters to trusted capability APIs, preserves an acyclic graph, exposes a board RSC surface to the route, and specifies owner authorization plus report-once handling.

The proposal coherently centralizes policy in a board use case, defines board-local ports and narrow adapters, keeps capability internals private, provides a thin board-only RSC path, and enforces authorization with single-boundary failure reporting.

Board ownership, acyclic capability separation, the board-only RSC flow, authorization, and report-once behavior are clear. Dependency inversion is only partial because board calls foreign published operations directly instead of defining board-language ports and adapters.

Board policy and orchestration are centralized, capability APIs are narrow, the graph is acyclic, and the page uses a board surface. It lacks board-owned dependency ports, and although authorization and inaccessible-label handling are addressed, unexpected-failure report-once behavior is not specified.
